get_my_guild_member.reason: Discord's spec omits BotToken here and it is correct to do so: this operation reads the *calling user's* member object, which only exists under an OAuth2 bearer with guilds.members.read. Recorded explicitly so the dispatcher refuses it under a bot profile with an accurate message rather than a bare 401.

get_current_user_application_entitlement.reason: OAuth2-only for the same reason: it reads entitlements belonging to the authorizing user, not the application.

get_application_user_role_connection.reason: Role connections are user-scoped metadata; a bot token has no user to scope to.

update_application_user_role_connection.reason: Role connections are user-scoped metadata; a bot token has no user to scope to.

delete_application_user_role_connection.reason: Role connections are user-scoped metadata; a bot token has no user to scope to.

get_guild.reason: Covered by a curated tool with a bounded, model-friendly projection.

prune_guild.reason: Discord's method (POST) understates this: it removes members in bulk and cannot be undone.

delete_guild.reason: Deletes an entire guild. Classified destructive rather than bot_admin so it can never be reached through the admin dispatcher without a preview token.

delete_user_guild.reason: Makes the bot leave a guild, which is irreversible without a fresh invite.
